title: Mark Rylance is the GOAT, like if you agree! 😂 👍🏻 #theatre #broadway ...
transcript: would you dress up as a fish for a free theatre ticket? well some people actually did back in 2016 when this West End play offered a unique ticket deal welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history so in 2016, Mark Rylance, the highly renowned but somewhat eccentric star of stage and screen had just won an Oscar and returned to the stage in a fittingly kooky play called Nice Fish he was also the co-writer of the play which essentially took a bunch of prose poems by the writer Louis Jenkins and used that as the script of the play except it was delivered by these two ice fishermen and the idea is that like while they're tediously waiting out in the cold for the fish to bite they're delivering these introspective monologues reflecting on life and fishing, etc. I found the show pretty charming and amusing although I do think it lost its steam after about an hour and ended up kinda going off the rails but anyway rather than offering regular rush tickets or day seats as they call them in London they came up with this very special deal they reserved four tickets per night in the box seats of the theatre and gave them away for free to anyone who showed up at the theatre at 6PM dressed as either a fish or a fisherman I was actually in London at the time and I considered taking advantage of this deal like just for the plot but I had actually already seen the show in New York earlier that year and I'm not one for repeats and for that matter I'm also not much of a costume person it kinda just felt like hassle which I guess is the point one of the few times in my life that I was not su-FISH-ently committed to the bit but what do you think would you go through all that trouble to see the legendary Mark Ryland on stage for free? real quick, before I finish I wanna recognize that the director of this play was Claire van Kampen who was not only a frequent collaborator of Mark Rylance’s but his wife of many years and she sadly passed away just earlier this year on Mark Rylance’s birthday no less so my heart goes out to them and their family
